stories.headline: Guardians survive in Chicago, head home with chance to advance
stories.summary: Jose Ramirez delivered again, homering and driving in three runs Thursday night to help the Guardians beat the White Sox 9-5 to send their ALDS to a decisive Game 5.
stories.body:
CHICAGO -- When it comes to tournaments, the cliche in sports is that you just need to survive and advance. After winning two long, ragged games in an electric ballpark, the Cleveland Guardians survived and then survived some more.

Now they'll get a chance to advance.

The Guardians came from behind twice in Game 4 on Thursday night, beating the Chicago White Sox 9-5 and forcing a winner-take-all Game 5 on Saturday in Cleveland. The Guardians arrived in Chicago down 2-0 in this American League Division Series.

"It's what we try to do as an organization," Guardians third baseman Jose Ramirez said through a club interpreter. "Try to always compete. Don't quit in any game. What this team is doing is only what we know how to do."

Ramirez and Patrick Bailey homered in the fifth inning in Cleveland's first comeback. Then after the White Sox retook the lead, the Guardians sent 10 batters to the plate while grinding out six runs in the sixth against Chicago's heavily used bullpen.

The White Sox never recovered.

"They're making really good swing decisions," Chicago manager Will Venable said. "They're making contact. We talked about how good a job they do of doing that. When you walk guys, they make you pay."

Both games in Chicago featured a raucous, jam-packed crowd at Rate Field, clad almost uniformly in black, hoping to see the White Sox clinch a postseason series at home for the first time since Oct. 14, 1906 -- six days shy of 120 years.

For now, the wait continues.

The gathering saw two terse, fairly ragged games that featured a lot of strikeouts, walks and hit batters, an ongoing battle of the strike zone that favored Cleveland. Over the two games combined, Guardians pitchers recorded 31 strikeouts to the White Sox's nine. Meanwhile, Cleveland's hitters drew 17 walks, six more than Chicago.

"That's just baseball, man," said Guardians outfielder Chase DeLauter, who, in addition to the win, was celebrating his 25th birthday. "Pitchers making good pitches, hitters hitting good pitches and taking good pitches. The more you control that on both sides of the ball puts you in a good spot to win the ballgame."

Both managers pulled out all the stops in Game 4, burning through 15 pitchers over nine innings. Cleveland got 2⅓ innings from standout rookie Parker Messick in the shortest start of his career to date. After six relievers followed Messick, Guardians manager Steven Vogt turned to probable Game 5 starter Gavin Williams to get the last three outs.

"The script tonight got ripped up in the third," Vogt said. "And when you have to go to the bullpen early, you've got to get creative in a win-or-go-home game."

Cleveland, which won 9-3 in Game 3 on Wednesday, became the sixth team to score at least nine runs in consecutive elimination games. It did it by controlling the strike zone even in an adrenalin-infused atmosphere, even when Chicago relief ace Grant Taylor came on in the sixth.

Taylor has become a sensation in Chicago for his often-dominant, versatile relief work, but on Thursday he didn't retire any of the six batters he faced, allowing four runs on five singles and a pair of walks.

"They just had good at bats, made me come to them," Taylor said. "Obviously two walks isn't going to get the job done. Then when I did come in the zone, they put the ball in play and good things happened for them."

Cleveland's approach was present up and down its lineup and even off the bench, as Bailey's solo blast came in a pinch-hitting spot. In many ways, the Guardians did a better job of channeling the amped-up energy of the gathering than the home team.

"The discussion was if we lose, we're gone," Bailey said. "Might as well go out there and win. We've still got one more to win at home."

With the road team having gone 4-for-4 in the series, the Guardians certainly can't rest on their accomplishments on the South Side. History is against Cleveland, which is 2-9 all-time in win-or-go-home games; the White Sox never have played such a contest during their long history, at least not in a multigame series.

For both teams, it might be a matter of which pitching staff has the most wherewithal remaining. According to ESPN research, Chicago has gotten 12⅔ innings from its starters during the playoffs, the fewest in history through a club's first six postseason games.

But Cleveland's staff has had to work just as hard, so when Saturday rolls around, expect a nail-biter. It will be another game of survivor with the winner this time advancing to the AL Championship Series to face the rested Tampa Bay Rays.

Game 5 will mark the 18th, and final, game between the AL Central opponents this season. Cleveland will be playing to break even in those contests by winning the one that matters most.

"I think it's going to be crazy," Ramirez said. "It's going to be an incredible energy. For us, it's going to be the same mindset: Try to win the game and enjoy the environment that's going to be at Progressive [Field]."

stories.headline: LeBron James scores 10 points in 18 minutes in 76ers debut
stories.summary: LeBron James, who joined the 76ers this summer, had 10 points, five assists and four rebounds in the first half of his debut with Philadelphia.
stories.body:
NEW YORK -- LeBron James sat at the same cubby he has for years in the visitors locker room at Barclays Center. His jersey still had No. 23 stitched on the front and back. And when he shook talcum powder into his hands at center court for his pregame chalk toss, throngs of fans held up their cell phones as they always have to record the ritual.

But Thursday night's game between Philadelphia 76ers and Brooklyn Nets was anything but old hat for the 24-year veteran who made his preseason debut with the fourth -- and likely last -- franchise of his career.

"I mean, it felt a little different," James said after Philadelphia's 114-108 loss. "Obviously, just wearing a new uniform, but the game is the game. ... And I was happy to be able to log some minutes with the guys that we've been going at each other in practice for the last two weeks."

It was also the preseason debut for the Sixers' planned starting lineup of Joel Embiid, Jaylen Brown, Tyrese Maxey and VJ Edgecombe flanking the 41-year-old star. The unit outscored the Nets by two points in the 10 minutes it was on the court in the first half.

James made an immediate impact with his passing, finding a streaking Edgecombe with a three-quarter-court feed to set up the second-year guard for a layup just more than a minute into the game.

"Someone like him just requires so much gravity and attracts so much attention that I just got to play off of him," said Edgecombe, who finished with 11 points. "And that's cutting, running the floor, spotting up, whatever. So, yeah, he just -- we made eye contact and I knew what that meant."

James played 18 minutes, all in the first half, and finished with 10 points, four rebounds and a team-high five assists. Philadelphia outscored Brooklyn by 10 in James' minutes.

He attempted only one field goal, which he made, and the rest of his points came at the foul line, where he went 8-for-8.

"He already got the [scoring] record," Edgecombe joked. "He don't care to score anymore."

During training camp last week, Sixers coach Nick Nurse said he looks at James' role not necessarily as a point forward but as an "offense creator" for Philadelphia.

He did plenty of creating for others against Brooklyn, with Brown (18 points on 5-for-9 shooting) and Maxey (14 points on 5-for-8 shooting) also reaching double digits.

"He's a great, great passer; it was certainly on display tonight," Nurse said. "There were a couple of long ones for layups, he threw some middle ones for layups and he threw some in the quarter court, guys cutting. ... It was good. I thought he really read the game well."

The one Sixers starter who struggled was Embiid, who scored just six points on 1-for-5 shooting and coughed up eight turnovers in 24 minutes.

"I got to do a better job of taking care of the ball," Embiid said. "But [it was the] first game. My first few games usually every year [are like this]. So yeah, it's going to take a few games to get going and just got to do a better job."

Still, Nurse said Embiid's mere inclusion after all the injuries that sidelined him the past few seasons was a positive.

"Obviously, he can play a lot better than that," Nurse said. "He'd be the first one to say. But also, I'm extremely happy he was out there with the group, and I thought he was playing very hard, which was great to see."

Brown said he and Embiid need to "figure some things out in terms of spacing" to help each other flow offensively.

They also need to avoid running into each other, as they did in the first half, when Embiid fell to the floor and Brown, trying to avoid him, also spilled onto the court.

"Flexed my knee a little bit, but it seems to be all right," Brown said.

Philadelphia has two preseason games remaining: at the Boston Celtics on Saturday and at home against Boston on Oct. 16.

Nurse said he plans to play his starters again in one of those two games and extend their minutes into the second half. Sources told ESPN that the starters are more likely to play in the finale.

For as different as it all feels for James right now, the Sixers showed flashes of familiarity with one another on the court -- which is what the preseason is for, especially for a group as new as this one.

"We're still trying to put each other in a position to be successful and complement each other the best way we can out on the floor," James said. "But it's going to take some time. Tonight was a good sample size for us to build on."

stories.headline: AFL player movement tracker: trade requests, free agency latest, who's on the move?
stories.summary: The offseason is upon us which means AFL trades, free agency, and player movement is about to take off. Here's the latest news, whispers, and confirmed deals.
stories.body:
It's AFL player movement season, with trades and free agency set to dominate the month of October. So who is going where? Keep track with our player movement guide here.

When is the AFL trade and free agency window?
The 2026 AFL trade period commences on Monday, October 5 and closes in the evening of Wednesday, October 14.

The free agency window opens and closes a little earlier; it runs from Friday, October 2 until Friday, October 9.

Friday, Oct. 9
Butters is a Bulldog

Zak Butters is officially a Western Bulldog. Port Adelaide will not match the offer and accept pick No. 5 as compensation, having also earlier secured picks 6, 10, and two future-firsts in the five-club mega trade. The star free agent and three-time All-Australian, who played 156 games and kicked 73 goals for the Power after being drafted in 2019, has signed a nine-year deal with his boyhood club

Hawks land spearhead King

After securing Zach Merrett earlier this week, Hawthorn have officially welcomed Ben King today after gold Coast elected not to match the offer for the restricted free agent. the Suns will receive a first round pick as compensation, which currently stands at pick No. 7.

Mega trade approved

The league approved a mega trade involving Port Adelaide, the Bulldogs, Melbourne, Hawthorn and Carlton, two players and scores of picks.

Under the five-team deal, the Bulldogs gave up picks No.12 and No.31 and a 2028 first-rounder to bring in Hawthorn's Finn Maginness, Carlton's Hudson O'Keeffe and later picks in this year's draft and future years.

Port parted with picks No.4, 46 and 81 and six second-round or worse future selections to get back picks No.6 and No.10, Melbourne's 2027 first-rounder and the Dogs' 2028 first-rounder.

The Demons surrendered picks No.6, 10 and 87 and their 2027 first-rounder -- as well as two late future picks -- for picks No.4, 12, 31 and 46.

Hawthorn (2027 third-rounder) and Carlton (2028 fourth-rounder) received late future picks for Maginness and O'Keeffe.

-- AAP

Flag Lion gets his wish

Brisbane has traded second-year Lion and 2025 premiership player Sam Marshall and pick No.39 to St Kilda for a 2027 first-rounder.

Thursday, Oct. 8
Marshall lands at the Cats

St Kilda have pulled the trigger on a deal to send contracted ruckman Rowan Marshall to Geelong, as the Cats and other rival clubs circle Sydney star Nick Blakey.

Geelong traded pick No.14 in this year's draft for the disenchanted 30-year-old and a third-round selection in 2028 on Thursday afternoon.

New Zealand-born Marshall had requested a move to the Cats for a second straight year after St Kilda recruited Tom De Koning to become their first-choice ruckman.

-- AAP

Wednesday, Oct. 7
Dons defender gets traded to the Cats

After being denied a trade last year, Jordan Ridley got his wish for a fresh start after Essendon and Geelong agreed to a deal on Wednesday.

Geelong gave up utility Jack Bowes, a 2027 first-round pick and 2028 second-round pick to get the 27-year-old Ridley through the door.

Pick No. 60 and a 2028 fourth-round selection will come back to the Cats from the Bombers.

--AAP

Tuesday, Oct. 6
O'Driscoll makes the move over east

Fremantle have traded 24-year-old Nathan O'Driscoll to Richmond in exchange for pick 61 in this year's draft.

The winger played 17 games for the Dockers this season but wasn't selected for the Grand Final.

Monday, Oct. 5
TRADE PERIOD OPENS
Merrett finally becomes a Hawk

After attempting to join Hawthorn last year, Zach Merrett has finally been traded from Essendon to the Hawks.

Hawthorn have sent picks 15, 25 and a 2028 second-round pick in exchange for the 31-year-old.

Merrett leaves the Bombers a week after winning a record-equaling seventh Crichton Medal, three All-Australian blazers, and 274 games.

Pendlebury becomes a Sun

AFL games record holder Scott Pendlebury is officially a Sun after Gold Coast and Collingwood agreed on a trade for the 38-year-old veteran.

Pendlebury, a two-time premiership player, heads to the Suns in exchange for pick No. 65 in this year's draft.

"It's an exciting group here at the SUNS and the opportunity to bring a few different ideas and also learn from a great group of coaches and players is one I'm really looking forward to," Pendlebury told the Suns.

"This side is one I've watched from afar and really admired. I've got a bit of knowledge about the industry so I'm here to play my role and help this squad continue to develop."

Jesse Hogan traded from GWS to Collingwood

Out-of-favour Giants forward Jesse Hogan has made the switch to Collingwood in exchange for pick 75.

The 31-year-old won the Coleman Medal in 2024 but has been unable to recapture his best form at the Giants in the two years since.

Magpies list boss Justin Leppitsch said Hogan would be a valuable addition.

"On behalf of everyone at Collingwood, I'd like to warmly welcome Jesse to Collingwood. Jesse has established himself as one of the competition's premier key forwards and we're excited to see him bring his experience and talent to our club," he said.

"His aerial presence inside forward-50 and his consistency as a goal-kicker make him a genuine threat.

"Like Lachie (Neale), Jesse has a passion to teach the next generation and will make a great addition to our club."

Saturday, Oct. 3
Bulldogs seal free-agency signing of key defender

The Western Bulldogs have finally snagged the key defender they need, securing Adelaide backman Jordon Butts as an unrestricted free agent.

The Bulldogs are set for a bumper AFL trade period headlined by working through a deal for Port Adelaide superstar Zak Butters, ahead of a 2027 season where the club will have high expectations.

But after seeing off Carlton's advances to keep hold of defender Buku Khamis, the Bulldogs have filled a major area of need by adding 26-year-old Butts.

Adelaide will receive a second-round compensation selection, currently pick No.33, in this year's draft.

-- AAP

Friday, Oct. 2
FREE AGENCY OPEN
Three-peat Lion locks in Magpies move

Lachie Neale has sealed his high-profile switch to Collingwood, with Brisbane teasing the dual Brownlow medallist on his way out the door.

The AFL approved Neale signing a three-year deal with the Magpies on Friday afternoon, closing out the first day of free agency.

The 33-year-old ball-winner leaves as an unrestricted free agent after the Lions clinched a third straight flag with their stunning seven-point grand final victory over Fremantle.

-- AAP

Greene on his way to the Cats

Toby Greene will join Geelong as an unrestricted free agent on a three-year deal, re-partnering with former Giants teammate Jeremey Cameron.

The paperwork was lodged to the AFL on Friday morning.

The Giants receive band three compensation for Greene, which is currently pick No. 26 in the upcoming draft.

Greene departs the Giants with his name etched in the club's record books, sitting first in games played for the club with a tally of 282 games, as well as leading the club's all-time goalkicking tally with 450 majors.

Briggs now a Tiger

Richmond has landed GWS ruck Kieren Briggs as an unrestricted free agent.

Briggs' move to the Tigers was confirmed just hours after the free agency window opened on Friday.

Briggs played 88 games for GWS after joining the club as the No.34 pick in the 2018 draft.

Amartey officially joins the Blues

Free agency has opened with a bang, with out-of-favour key forward Joel Amartey committing to Carlton.

Details are still to come on the length of contract, and Sydney's compensation.

Hawthorn father-son recommits despite interest

Calsher Dear has made a shock decision to re-sign with the Hawks for two years, despite being out of favour thorughout 2026.

The 20-year-old has kicked 39 goals from 31 games, but found himself behind Jack Gunston, Mitch Lewis and Mabior Chol. With Gunston signed on and Suns forward Ben King expected to sign with the Hawks as well, there were questions about whether Dear would get enough opportunity at his childhood club.

Hawks list boss Mark McKenzie said the club was "really pleased" that Dear had recommitted.

"He remains an important part of what we are trying to achieve as a club," he said.

"Following his debut season, Calsher showed us all the special talent that he is, but as a key tall at 21 years of age, we've needed to be patient with his progression.

"Having battled several injuries over his first three seasons in the system, we are very excited about what the future holds for Calsher with a strong pre-season under his belt and greater continuity into 2027 and beyond."

Thursday, Oct. 1
Goater set to make cross-city switch

North Melbourne defender Josh Goater is set to join the Hawks after requesting a trade on Thursday.

Having played just 18 games, the 23-year-old had fallen out of favour after an injury-hit run in his time at North.

Premiership Lion requests trade

The Brisbane Lions have confirmed Sam Marshall has requested a trade to St Kilda.

"The Brisbane Lions confirm premiership midfielder Sam Marshall has requested to be traded to St Kilda," the Lions said in a statement.

"Marshall has played 13 games, including the 2025 Premiership, across two seasons since being selected in the first round of the 2024 draft as a graduate of the Youi Brisbane Lions Academy.

"The club respects Marshall's request to be traded, and will work towards facilitating an outcome that best reflects true value to the Brisbane Lions for the 20-year-old."

Tuesday, Sept. 29
Neale informs Lions he intends to join Collingwood

Two-time Brownlow Medal winner Lachie Neale has told Brisbane he will depart the club as an unrestricted free agent and sign a three-year deal with Collingwood.

Aware that Neale intended to leave at the end of the year, the Lions never offered him a new contract.

The paperwork for the deal is expected to be formalised as early as Friday when the free agency period opens.

Friday, Sept. 25
Jordon Butts to join the Bulldogs

Zak Butters isn't the only South Australian-based player keen to join the Western Bulldogs, with Crows' key defender Jordon Butts officially naming the Dogs as his preferred offseason destination.

The unrestricted free agent will sign a five-year deal at the Kennel, according to AFL.com.au.

Tuesday, Sept. 22
Amartey officially names Carlton

Wantaway Sydney forward Joel Amartey has confirmed his desire to join Carlton as an unrestricted free agent.

The 26-year-old was kept out of the Swans' side with an Achilles injury in the latter stages of the year.

With Charlie Curnow (75 goals in 2026) and Logan McDonald (51) cementing their spots in the Sydney forward line as the prime targets, Amartey is hoping for more opportunity at the Blues.

Thursday, Sept. 17
GWS captain finally makes big call on his future

Toby Greene has opted to leave GWS, telling the AFL club he wishes to play with Geelong next season. Greene, who has been at the Giants since their foundation season in 2012, wants to go back to Victoria for family reasons.

In an extraordinary way to announce the decision, outgoing GWS boss Dave Matthews confirmed Greene's intentions on radio, before the club released a statement.

The 32-year-old has been offered a lucrative three-year deal to join the Cats.

Saturday, Sept. 12
Zak Butters makes huge free agency call
The year's hottest restricted free agent Zak Butters has made a huge call on his future, nominating the Western Bulldogs as his preferred destination.

After a year of speculation, with Geelong thought to be the front-runner for the Power star's signature, Butters made the call on Saturday, first reported by AFL.com.au's Callum Twomey.

The deal is reportedly for nine years.

Thursday, Sept. 10
Hogan set to join Pies
GWS and Collingwood have both confirmed that 2024 Coleman Medal winner Jesse Hogan has chosen the Magpies at his next home.

Set to be a four-club player, Hogan is 31 and coming off a 12-goal season from just nine appearances.

It's a big boost for the Magpies if Hogan can recapture his form; key forward has been an area of concern for a number of years.

Tuesday, Sept. 8
Bailey set to be Lion for life
Brisbane's Zac Bailey has ended months of 'will he, won't he' speculation to sign with the Lions for eight years, taking him through the 2034 season, the the club confirmed on Tuesday.

Bailey, a free agent, had been a big target for the Crows, who had reportedly tabled a more lucrative offer.

"I'm absolutely rapt to be staying at the Brisbane Lions," Bailey said in a statement.

"I love the environment here, the players, coaches and staff who all make it a great place to be and I feel like this Club continues to bring the best out of me.

"This Club means so much to me - I came here as a young player and have grown up here and to know I will be here long-term is something I'm really proud of.

"I would like to thank the club, my partner Em, my family and my management for being so supportive throughout this process.

"I love what we as a club have achieved during my time here and I am super excited about what we can continue to achieve together."

Rowan Marshall requests trade
St Kilda ruck Rowan Marshall looks set to be on the move, with the Saints confirming the big man had requested a trade for the second straight season.

While Marshall hasn't requested a specific club, it's likely to be Geelong after he failed to secure a trade to the Cats last year. He played 21 games for the Saints this seaosn, juggling ruck duties with Tom De Koning, who came in from Carlton last offseason.

"Rowan is a highly valued member of the St Kilda Football Club and remains contracted until the end of 2027," the Saints said in a statement.

"Marshall has not nominated a preferred destination at this stage, with the club making clear that any trade will need to be in the best interests of the St Kilda Football Club."

Zane Duursma wants to go to Melbourne
The No. 4 pick in the 2023 AFL draft Zane Duursma has requested a trade out of North Melbourne, with Melbourne in his sights.

The news comes a week after coach Alastair Clarkson was sacked by the club. North won nine games in 2026, their best return since 2019.

Ed Allan re-signs with the Pies
After speculation about his future at the Magpies, mdifielder Ed Allan has put pen to paper, signing a four year extension to remain at Collingwood.

2026 was a breakout season for Allan, who played 19 games and averaged a career-high 16.5 disposals per game.

Monday, Sept. 7
Pair of in-demand Dogs re-sign
According to afl.com.au, both Arty Jones and Buku Khamis will remain at the Kennel this offseason.

Jones will sign a three-year deal, while Khamis has a five-year contract in front of him.

Essendon and Brisbane had interest in livewire forward Jones, who had a standout performance against Collingwood in the wildcard final win, while the Blues were heavily linked to Khamis for a second straight offseason.

Cooper Hodge nomintes Hawthorn
A big boost for the Hawks, with club champion Luke Hodge's son Cooper choosing to join the Melbourne-based team as a father-son at this year's draft.

He had the option of going to Brisbane as a Lions academy member.

stories.body:
From Breanna Stewart to Cynthia Cooper, the list of women who have been named WNBA Most Valuable Player includes some of the most accomplished players in the history of women's basketball.

A national panel of 60 sportswriters and broadcasters vote on the WNBA's annual regular-season awards, including MVP, Defensive Player of the Year, Rookie of the Year, Sixth Player of the Year, Most Improved Player, Coach of the Year and the All-WNBA, All-Defensive and All-Rookie teams. In 2026, A'ja Wilson became the first player in league history to win the honor five times.

stories.headline: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander joins athletes who became owners
stories.summary: The Oklahoma City Thunder star joins a list of athletes that includes LeBron James, Serena Williams, Wayne Gretzky and Tom Brady.
stories.body:
Shai Gilgeous-Alexander is getting into the ownership game.

On Thursday, Spanish soccer giants Atlético Madrid announced that the Oklahoma City Thunder guard would be joining the club as an investor.

"I am excited to officially join the group of shareholders of Atlético de Madrid," Gilgeous-Alexander said in the club's post. "This is a club with a long history at the top of European football, and I am grateful for the opportunity to be part of its future."

The NBA superstar is far from the first athlete, active or former, to enter the ownership sphere. Here are other athletes who are now team owners:

Jason Kidd -- Everton

In April 2025, English Premier League club Everton announced that then-Dallas Mavericks coach Jason Kidd would be adding a different title to his résumé: ownership group member. The news came after Kidd joined Roundhouse Capital Holdings, which is part of the Friedkin Group -- the U.S. firm that completed its takeover of Everton's ownership the previous December.

Vince Carter, Tracy McGrady, Jozy Altidore -- Buffalo Bills

In December 2024, the Bills announced Carter, McGrady and Altidore were among 10 limited partners the team was adding to its ownership group. Both McGrady (New York Knicks) and Altidore (New York Red Bulls) played for New York-area teams, while Carter spent time with the Brooklyn Nets (who were known as the New Jersey Nets at the time) and was McGrady's teammate on the Toronto Raptors (who are closer to Buffalo than NYC-based teams).

Tom Brady -- Las Vegas Aces, Las Vegas Raiders, Birmingham City

The Las Vegas Aces, the reigning WNBA champions, have added to their championship credentials. Seven-time Super Bowl champion Tom Brady acquired a minority stake in the team whose majority owner is Las Vegas Raiders owner Mark Davis.

"I have always been a huge fan of women's sports, and I admire the work that the Aces' players, staff, and the WNBA continue to do to grow the sport and empower future generations of athletes," Brady said in a statement. "To be able to contribute in any way to that mission as a member of the Aces organization is an incredible honor."

Brady attended an Aces game in May 2022 and sent gifts to star Kelsey Plum. Plum and other Aces players were excited to have Brady as part of the team.

He also added the Las Vegas Raiders to his resume after his purchase of minority stake in the franchise was approved by NFL teams owners on Tuesday. The deal was agreed on in May 2023, but it took owners 17 months to give their approval over concerns he was receiving too much of a discount from majority owner Mark Davis.

Brady is also a minority owner of Birmingham City, a club in English soccer's second-tier Championship.

Lewis Hamilton -- Denver Broncos

The Broncos' ownership group added racing royalty in August 2022. Formula One driver Lewis Hamilton has a stake with the Walton-Penner group, which purchased the team in June 2022.

Hamilton, 37, has the Formula One record for most race wins and has won the Formula One title seven times. The ownership group, which purchased the team for $4.65 billion, is led by Walmart heir Rob Walton and includes former U.S. Secretary of State Condoleezza Rice, who also has a stake.

In April, Hamilton joined with Serena Williams in a consortium led by former Liverpool chairman Martin Broughton in an attempt to buy Premier League club Chelsea.

"He is a champion competitor who knows what it takes to lead a winning team," Walton said in a statement.

Marshawn Lynch -- Seattle Kraken

Lynch spent 13 seasons in Seattle with the Seahawks, but his new sports venture in the state of Washington is on the ice. On April 18, he joined the Seattle Kraken ownership team as a minority investor. The former NFL running back will be a part of the NHL's "Hockey is for Everyone" campaign and Kraken owner Tod Leiweke said Lynch expressed interest in shadowing him to learn hockey CEO operations.

"This is something I never would have imagined," Lynch said to CNBC in a statement. "I always dreamed of playing on a professional team but owning one is something special. As I look back on some of my accomplishments...I'm [going to] continue to count my blessings."

Grammy Award-winning artist and Seattle native Macklemore also joined the Kraken ownership team with Lynch.

Wayne Gretzky, Steve Nash and Dustin Johnson -- Las Vegas Desert Dogs

Wayne Gretzky is a big lacrosse guy? Yep, you read that right. The Great One may have made his name on the ice, but before Gretzky was the pride of the Edmonton Oilers he was a bona fide lax bro.

"The national sport of Canada is box lacrosse," Gretzky said. "I started playing lacrosse on a team at the age of six and played all the way until I was 16 years old. I have a great love for the game in the sense I really think that box lacrosse was such a crucial part of the success I ultimately had in ice hockey."

Because of this, it shouldn't be completely surprising that the hockey legend is linking up with 2020 Masters champion Dustin Johnson, NBA Hall of Famer and current Brooklyn Nets head coach Steve Nash and Nets owner Joe Tsai as part of a star-studded ownership group for the National Lacrosse League's newest expansion team in Las Vegas, the Desert Dogs.

Dwyane Wade -- Utah Jazz

Seeing Dwyane Wade support any team other than the Miami Heat is decidedly jarring. In April, the three-time NBA champion purchased an ownership stake in the Utah Jazz, joining majority owner and team governor Ryan Smith, and expressed a desire to take an active role in the franchise. D. Wade made good on his promise. He could be seen courtside throughout the season; he took action when an unsettling fan incident went down during the postseason, and he became a mentor to then-Jazz star Donovan Mitchell.

The former Miami Heat star also added to his portfolio with something a bit closer to home. Wade, a Chicago native, joined the ownership group of the WNBA's Chicago Sky.

"It's a great opportunity to be a part of the league in its very early stages. ... Growth is going to happen, and so I want to be a part of the growth of this league," Wade said.

Kevin Durant -- Philadelphia Union, NJ/NY Gotham FC

In June 2020, Brooklyn Nets star Kevin Durant purchased a 5% stake in MLS' Philadelphia Union, and he has an option to purchase an additional 5% at a later date. Durant also had engaged in talks about purchasing part of D.C. United the year prior, but he said the discussion never progressed.

Durant expanded his portfolio in May of this year, after being named as a minority owner of the National Women's Soccer League (NWSL) club NJ/NY Gotham FC.

Thirty Five Ventures (35V), a company co-founded by the two-time NBA champion and entrepreneur Rich Kleiman, made a significant investment to acquire a stake in the club, marking the company's second investment in a professional soccer team.

Renee Montgomery -- Atlanta Dream

Former Atlanta Dream guard Renee Montgomery made history in February as part of a three-member investor group that was approved to purchase the team. Montgomery is the first former player to become both an owner and executive of a WNBA franchise. The ownership change followed pressure on former Republican Sen. Kelly Loeffler to sell her share of the Dream, after she angered WNBA players with her opposition to the league's racial justice initiatives.

Patrick Mahomes -- Kansas City Royals

Patrick Mahomes is no stranger to winning. While the Kansas City Royals can't exactly say the same, you can't rule out that the quarterback's winning ways might rub off on the franchise now that he is part of their ownership group. If Mahomes' status as an icon in Kansas City was in question (it wasn't), this move surely cemented it. Becoming a baseball owner made sense on several levels for the Chiefs' QB1. Not only was Mahomes -- who played baseball in college -- a legitimate pro prospect, his father, Pat Mahomes, spent 11 seasons in Major League Baseball. He also had to find some way to put that $503 million contract extension to good use.

Venus and Serena Williams -- Miami Dolphins, Angel City FC

Winning major titles and making history, that's what the Williams sisters do. In 2009, Venus and Serena became the first Black female minority owners in the NFL by purchasing a part of the Miami Dolphins. Musicians Jimmy Buffett, Gloria and Emilio Estefan, Fergie and Marc Anthony also bought shares in the team -- the Dolphins' ownership group is nothing if not eclectic. Then, last year, Serena Williams became part of the star-studded Angel City FC ownership group bringing a NWSL team to Los Angeles in 2022.

Mia Hamm, Abby Wambach and Julie Foudy -- Angel City FC

When Angel City FC arrived on the scene it did so in style. Before we even knew the Los Angeles based NWSL club's name, we knew it had superstar backing like no other. Among the 14 former USWNT players who are part of the group are Mia Hamm, Abby Wambach and Julie Foudy. I would have named Lauren Holiday, Shannon Boxx, Rachel Buehler, Amanda Cromwell, Joy Fawcett, Tisha Venturini Hoch, Angela Hucles, Shannon MacMillan, Saskia Webber and sisters Lorrie Fair Allen and Ronnie Fair Sullins, but I was really trying to stay true to my whole "I'm only going to name 20 athletes" thing from the intro. There are also a bunch of celebrities in the mix, but we don't have that kind of time.

Michael Jordan -- Charlotte Hornets

While we're on the subject of owners who haven't had the type of success we grew accustomed to in their playing days, I would be remiss if I didn't mention the GOAT. In 2010, Michael Jordan became the first ex-player to be a majority owner in the league when the NBA's Board of Governors unanimously approved his $275 million bid to buy the then Charlotte Bobcats in his home state of North Carolina. After a decade of underwhelming years, things look to be on the up for the now Hornets with Rookie of the Year LaMelo Ball providing a long-awaited spark in the organization. Never forget when his dad said he could beat MJ one-on-one ... good times.

Alex Rodriguez -- Minnesota Timberwolves, Minnesota Lynx

I don't know what part of this purchase feels less ideal to me, that Alex Rodriguez and his 50-50 business partner Marc Lore are only pursuing acquiring the Minnesota Timberwolves and Lynx after their original plan to buy the New York Mets failed or that Timberwolves star Anthony Edwards had no idea who former MLB star A-Rod was. Either way, the $1.5 billion deal is expected to close around July 1.

David Beckham -- Inter Miami

David Beckham, iconic soccer player and remains-to-be-seen owner. Beckham -- who is incredibly hands on with the franchise -- is part of an ownership group which was initially called Miami Beckham United but now operates under the name Miami Freedom Park LLC. Beckham and Inter Miami have seemingly been riddled with controversy since the club's inception in 2018. But all those problems could be a thing of the past if Lionel Messi decides to head to MLS. Hey, stranger things have happened.

LeBron James -- Liverpool

Back in 2011, LeBron James and manager Maverick Carter became minority owners of Premier League club Liverpool after Fenway Sports Group, which purchased the team in 2010, became the sole marketer of James' global rights. The deal has turned out to be pretty lucrative for James -- his original stake in the club, valued at about $6.5 million, had grown to about $32 million as of 2018. In 2019, Liverpool won the Premier League for their first top-flight league title in thirty years.

James Harden -- Houston Dynamo, Houston Dash

James Harden might not be in Houston anymore, but the former Rockets superstar's presence is still felt in the city. The Beard purchased a 5% stake in the group that controls MLS' Houston Dynamo and NWSL's Houston Dash in 2019. Boxer Oscar De La Hoya is also part of the group. The Dash won their first NWSL title last year, so he's probably feeling pretty good about that investment.

Russell Wilson and Ken Griffey Jr. -- Seattle Sounders

What do Russell Wilson, Ken Griffey Jr. and Macklemore have in common? They are all part of the Seattle Sounders' ownership group. Wilson, along with his wife, musician Ciara, purchased a stake in the team in 2019 -- just in time for them to win an MLS Cup title. Griffey Jr. and his family followed suit in November 2020.

Zlatan Ibrahimovic -- Hammaraby

Seemingly everything Zlatan does makes people react intensely, and that remained true when he purchased part of Swedish team Hammaraby back in 2019. Fans of Malmo, another Swedish team where Zlatan started his professional career, reacted by vandalizing a statue of Zlatan outside the team's home stadium, placing a toilet seat around one of its arms.

Magic Johnson -- Los Angeles Dodgers

Big LA guy. In 2012, Lakers great Magic Johnson was part of a group that bought the Los Angeles Dodgers from Frank McCourt for a record $2 billion. At the time, the price shattered the mark for a sports franchise. Magic kept it real at the time of purchase when explaining his role in recruiting free agents, saying that while he can't talk hitting or pitching with players, he "can talk winning." If recent history is any indication (in case you blacked out all of 2020 -- the Dodgers won the World Series), it worked.

stories.headline: Jake Paul cleared to fight; Canelo, Strickland, others on wish list
stories.summary: Jake Paul, who has been cleared to resume fighting after recovering from a broken jaw, has a list of big names he'd like to face in boxing and MMA now that he's back.
stories.body:
Jake Paul has been medically cleared to return to boxing.

Paul (12-2, seven KOs), 29, has not fought since he suffered a broken jaw during his knockout loss to Anthony Joshua last December. Paul underwent surgical procedures on his jaw in December and February. Nakisa Bidarian, co-founder of Paul's Most Valuable Promotions, officially updated Paul's status Thursday.

"Jake Paul has been cleared to return to the boxing ring," Bidarian wrote on X.

Paul told ESPN in April that he'd resumed light training but had not been cleared to spar. He has targeted a full return to competition in early 2027.

In connection to the update on his health, Paul provided his latest wish list of eventual fights this week. The list included 15 potential fights, including Canelo Alvarez, Ryan Garcia, Francis Ngannou, Deontay Wilder in boxing as well as mixed martial arts contests against Conor McGregor and Nate Diaz.

The list also included UFC middleweight champion Sean Strickland (31-7), who linked himself to Paul this week in a series of online posts expressing frustration about his UFC contract.

"I gotta be honest, unless things change with the UFC I'm kinda over it," Strickland wrote on X. "McGregor makes 30 million to fight for 30 seconds and they don't want to pay us a fraction of it. Contemplating just going to 205 [pounds], knocking out my contract and scrapping with [Jake Paul]. That sounds fun."

Paul, who has been vocal for years along with MVP in encouraging the UFC to increase its fighter pay, acknowledged Strickland's post in a response.

"Sean Strickland I see your texts but are you out of contract?" Paul wrote. "Tell your 'promoter' to call MVP."

stories.headline: Harry Kane interest in MLS 'fulfilment of a dream' - commissioner
stories.summary: MLS commissioner Don Garber would love Harry Kane to follow Lionel Messi across the pond and says the England skipper's interest helps fulfil a dream that Sir David Beckham kept alive.
stories.body:
MLS commissioner Don Garber would love Harry Kane to follow Lionel Messi across the pond and says the England skipper's interest helps fulfil a dream that Sir David Beckham kept alive.

The 33-year-old is in the running for the Ballon d'Or having scored 73 goals for club and country in a season that saw the striker win the Bundesliga with Bayern Munich before World Cup bronze.

Kane shows no signs of slowing and he marked his record-equalling 125th England appearance by extending his international goal tally to 91 in Tuesday's 3-0 Nations League win against Czechia.

The striker scored six goals across a four-match camp that began with him revealing his interest in eventually moving to MLS as the striker spoke about his dreams of being an NFL kicker.

"I'd love for him to do that," commissioner Garber said. "I think, for me, it is the fulfilment of the dream that we had to build a proper soccer league that would drive a soccer nation. That sounds colloquial but actually we have that written down.

"We wanted to create something that would have the Harry Kanes of the world say 'I'd kind of like to play in MLS.' And I think Messi proved that.

"That was a competitive process, working to ensure that we had a dynamic that would be better than going back to Barca, working a dynamic that would not have him want to play in Saudi Arabia.

"Play in Miami, have them be able to build a new stadium and have him set records and be an MVP, and then have an unbelievable goodbye [this week] from his international career."

Garber welcomes Kane's keenness to move to MLS and is eternally grateful to another England captain as he prepares to step down from the post of commissioner he has held since 1999.

Beckham's move to LA Galaxy acted as the catalyst for the league's growth, which only accelerated when the former midfielder helped form Inter Miami and sign Argentina great Messi in 2023.

"I don't think I would say one is more important than the other," Garber said of the star duo's impact.

"David put this league on the path to credibility and respect. In the prime of his career, he came to LA.

"He came into Major League Soccer and showed the world that this league can be competitive, it could be respected, it could be fun, it could have great players.

"It attracted [Thierry] Henry and many, many other players right after that, so without David there's probably no Major League Soccer.

"That being said, Major League Soccer would not be the global phenomenon and not be sort of on the hearts and minds of just about anybody in the world without Leo Messi."

Garber will become chairman at the turn of the year and is proud of his legacy with MLS, which was founded as part of the bid to hold the 1994 World Cup in a country that has just co-hosted the largest edition of the tournament.

- England Nations League takeaways: Kane makes history, Tuchel steadies ship

The 68-year-old says they have made the planet's "biggest commercial market for the sport" during that time and is excited to see how they build on firm foundations.

"We just went from a country road, now we're getting onto the highway," Garber told the Press Association. "And we've got to get better.

"We have to have a league that is more competitive, that has an ability to get into the Club World Cup and win games. Miami won one.

"Not just be there but have people think that an MLS team can compete against other clubs in the world."

stories.headline: Mikel Arteta: 'I still have the scar' from Arsenal's Champions League final defeat
stories.summary: Mikel Arteta has said he still has a "scar" from Arsenal's Champions League final defeat to Paris Saint-Germain in May.
stories.body:
Mikel Arteta has said he still has a "scar" from Arsenal's Champions League final defeat to Paris Saint-Germain in May.

The Spaniard, whose new four-year contract at the Emirates was announced on Wednesday, took the club to their first Champions League final for 20 years last season but saw his team defeated on penalties after a 1-1 draw.

Echoing the words of the last man to take them to the brink of elite European glory -- Arsène Wenger, who previously said that "every defeat is a scar in your heart" -- Arteta told The Athletic: "I still have the scar, like Arsène says.

"I still have that poison in my veins. It has to stay there because that's when you learn and that probably is going to be a massive driver for me and everybody."

Looking towards the future, Arteta added that he was excited for a number of different aspects of the club's growth.

"Globally, with our supporters? Great. How are we going to build the next three squads? Great. How the rules of the game are going to change us, and how we're going to stay ahead of that to take advantage? Great," he said.

"But this is going to happen if every single day we look after what we built. We make it a little bit better, like software that is upgrading and upgrading. When can it stop is infinite."

He added: "It feels like it's still a lot to do, and it's just the beginning."

Arteta has, however, already managed to do something no Arsenal manager had achieved for 22 years: win a league title.

"It wasn't just a trophy. It was a moment that we're going to remember for the rest of our lives," he said.

Asked what game from his Arsenal tenure he would relive, the 44-year-old chose the controversial 1-0 win over West Ham which put the Gunners on the brink of returning to the top of the perch.

"This is football elevated to its best version, when a journey, a moment that can change so many people's lives, goes one way or the other," he said. "You just pray because you know if it goes the wrong side, probably it's gone again.

"That day when I went home, I said, 'We're going to be champions. It is our year. This has happened for a reason, and we're going to get it done.'"

Arsenal return from the international break in Saturday's early kickoff against Leeds United at the Emirates, looking to return to the top of the table ahead of Manchester City's trip to Liverpool on Sunday.

stories.headline: NRL: Spencer Leniu signs with Eels after early Roosters release
stories.summary: Spencer Leniu has signed a four-year deal with Parramatta just days after winning his fourth NRL premiership with the Sydney Roosters.
stories.body:
Spencer Leniu has signed a four-year deal with Parramatta just days after winning his fourth NRL premiership with the Sydney Roosters.

Leniu finished his three-year stint at the Tricolours on a high after a stellar performance in their 19-18 win over Newcastle to secure the 2026 trophy.

The NSW Origin representative added the Roosters' premiership ring to the three he won with Penrith from 2021-2023.

Leniu was granted a release from the final year of his Roosters contract, which will give the club some salary cap reprieve

The hard-hitting forward's Eels contract is reportedly worth more than the $850,000 per year he was making with Easts, where he spent much of his time coming off the bench.

He is expected to play a more active role in blue and gold, leading the line for the Eels' forward pack.

The westward move will see the former Panther reunite with good friend Jarome Luai, but first the pair will both suit up for Toa Samoa at the Rugby League World Cup.

Eels general manager of football Mark O'Neill shared his delight at signing one of the game's "premier enforcers".

"We're thrilled to have Spencer join the Parramatta Eels and become part of what we're building at this club," O'Neill said in a statement.

"He's one of the elite middle forwards in the game and has consistently performed on the biggest stages throughout his career.

The exit of Leniu adds to the exodus of stars from the Roosters premiership lineup.

Angus Crichton and Mark Nawaqanitawase are rugby-bound, Daly Cherry-Evans is joining Hull FC, while Daniel Tupou retired this week after his 307-game career.

Connor Watson, who missed the title decider due to concussion, has signed for a season with St George Illawarra Dragons.

Roosters coach Trent Robinson said Leniu had been a strong contributor during his time at the club.

"Spencer has brought a lot to our group over the last three years, both through the way he plays and the energy and personality he brings every day," Robinson said in a statement on Thursday.

"He brings an intensity and competitiveness to everything he does, and he challenges the people around him to be better.

"To see him finish his time here as a premiership winner is something he should be really proud of, and something we'll always share together."

With his departure announced at the Roosters' awards night on Wednesday, Leniu said he would leave the club on a high.

""I'm proud to have worn the Roosters jersey and I'll always have a lot of love and respect for the club, the boys and everyone who has supported me during my time here," said Leniu.

"Winning a premiership with this group and sharing that with the boys, our families and everyone at the club is something I'll carry with me for the rest of my life."

stories.headline: MLB division series 2026: Takeaways and analysis from ALDS Game 4
stories.summary: The ALDS is headed back to Cleveland! Here's how Game 4 went down and what it means.
stories.body:
The Cleveland Guardians are back in business.

With a second consecutive win on the South Side over the Chicago White Sox on Thursday night, the Guardians tied the American League Division Series, sending it back to Cleveland for a winner-take-all Game 5 on Saturday. A spot in the AL Championship Series against the Tampa Bay Rays is at stake.

Here's what Cleveland's latest victory means -- and how it went down.

Key links: Mega-preview | Series outlooks | Bracket | Schedule

Takeaways

Cleveland Guardians 9, Chicago White Sox 5
Series tied at 2

It was over when ... the Guardians put up six runs in the sixth inning, thanks to an implosion by the White Sox bullpen -- something we haven't seen all postseason. Jordan Hicks, Anthony Kay and Grant Taylor all gave up runs, as Cleveland peppered them with three consecutive bases-loaded singles to help put the game away. For the second night in a row, Jose Ramirez led the charge, hitting a home run and driving in three.

Stat that defined the game: The vaunted White Sox bullpen pitched 4⅔ innings in the middle of the game, giving up all nine runs.

Star who defined the game: Pitchers seem to have forgotten who Ramirez is. Yes, he is coming off his worst season in a decade. Yes, the power that has helped him morph from speedy spark plug to future Hall of Famer was sapped following a broken hamate bone in June. It returned in magnificent fashion Thursday in Cleveland's must-win Game 4.

With the Guardians trailing 2-1, Ramirez took a 99.9 mph, top-of-the-zone sinker from Hicks and tomahawked it into the right-field stands to stake Cleveland to a 3-2 lead. The bat speed, the bat control, the timing -- it was all there in the moment Cleveland needed Ramirez most. Another RBI on an infield single with the bases loaded helped key the Guardians' six-run sixth inning. With a winner-takes-all Game 5 coming Saturday, Ramirez is finding the best version of himself again. Precisely when the Guardians need it.

What it means for the rest of the series: Game 5 sets up as more of a traditional starter-versus-starter contest. The Guardians are expected to send Gavin Williams (who got the final three outs of Game 4) to the mound and the White Sox will counter with Sean Burke. Chicago's bullpen is taxed, so a day off will help -- but it's hard to know who Chicago can rely on after this Game 4 debacle. -- Jeff Passan and Jesse Rogers

stories.headline: Buccaneers explode in third quarter against Cowboys to get first win
stories.summary: Undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels and Tampa Bay held off Dallas on "Thursday Night Football."
stories.body:
ARLINGTON, Texas -- The Tampa Bay Buccaneers went into halftime trailing by three points against the Dallas Cowboys on Thursday, and then they exploded in the third quarter for 17 points to take an 11-point lead en route to a 24-16 win on the road.

Inside linebacker Alex Anzalone picked off Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott's pass with 1:22 to go to preserve the Bucs' first win of the season. The fact that it was Anzalone, who has struggled to assimilate into coach Todd Bowles' defense and has faced a ton of criticism for it, put a bow on things after coming into Week 5 as the only winless team in the NFC.

The Bucs hadn't won a Thursday night road game since beating the Philadelphia Eagles on Oct. 14, 2021, when Tom Brady was Tampa's QB. On Thursday, undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels made his second straight start at quarterback as Baker Mayfield recovers from a dislocated right thumb that he suffered in Week 3.

The Bucs also ran for 241 yards, led by Bucky Irving's 165 on 21 carries. Irving also ran for a touchdown and caught another.

If there were complaints for the Bucs, it would be Bowles' decision to go for it on fourth-and-goal from the 1-yard line with Sean Tucker's run being stuffed with 8:36 left in the fourth quarter instead of kicking a field goal to go up by 17. That gave Dallas life before Anzalone's interception closed the door. The Bucs also had a staggering 14 penalties, but they capitalized on three Cowboys turnovers.

Here are the most important things to know from Thursday night for both teams:

Tampa Bay Buccaneers (1-4)
QB breakdown: Remember that double mug blitz that doomed Daniels and the offensive line on the final drive last week against the Green Bay Packers? The Cowboys showed it on third-and-4 of the Bucs' first possession, and Daniels fired a 6-yard completion to Emeka Egbuka before finding Irving in the flat for a 5-yard touchdown. Daniels completed 19 of 25 passes for 189 passing yards and a touchdown. Daniels' arm also came alive with the deep ball -- something we've seldom seen this season from him or Mayfield -- connecting with wide receiver Tez Johnson on a corner route for a 64-yard reception.

Biggest surprise: Heading into this game, Bucs opponents were completing 63.8% of their passes against Bowles' blitzing schemes. But on Thursday night, Prescott started out by completing 2 of 13 passes against the blitz (15.4%) through three quarters. He finished 9-of-20 (45%), but it was too little, too late. In the absence of All-Pro safety Antoine Winfield Jr., Tykee Smith had arguably his best game, recording five quarterback pressures on seven blitzes. He also bobbled a potential interception that Yaya Diaby ultimately corralled. Cornerback Jacob Parrish had three pass breakups and allowed just one reception, while Zyon McCollum gave up just two.

Stat to know: Irving delivered a 72-yard rush -- the longest of his career and longest by a Buccaneer since Ronald Jones II had a 98-yard run in Week 10 of the 2020 season. What was particularly impressive about the run was the offensive line finally gained some synergy in Zac Robinson's offense, gaining 64 rushing yards before contact on the play. -- Jenna Laine

Next game: vs. Pittsburgh Steelers (Oct. 18)

Dallas Cowboys (2-3)
There are good losses, bad losses and cataclysmic losses.

Thursday's loss to the Buccaneers is one of the worst in recent memory in part because the Buccaneers entered the game 0-4, starting an undrafted rookie quarterback and missing one of their best defenders (Winfield).

An offense that wants to be called the "Greatest Offense There Is" was inept after the first drive. After a 70-yard touchdown drive to open the game that included five first downs, the Cowboys' next seven drives gained 152 yards (48 on one play) and seven first downs as a 10-7 lead turned into a 24-10 deficit in the third quarter.

And the defense once again was shredded, although this time it was Daniels through the air and Irving on the ground. For the 12th straight time, dating back to last year, the Cowboys allowed 20 or more points in a game, matching a team record. They gave up a 72-yard run and a 64-yard pass, while allowing a first down on third-and-21. All in the second half.

As good as the Cowboys could have felt after Sunday's come-from-behind win at the Houston Texans, this loss was embarrassing for a team that fancied itself a contender.

Prescott finished the night 24-of-32 for 316 passing yards and a touchdown -- and George Pickens had nine catches for 130 yards and a touchdown -- but the two interceptions hurt.

Trend to watch: Daniels had a passer rating of 110.2, as the Cowboys' defense has allowed opposing quarterbacks to post a passer rating of at least 99.1 in the first five weeks. Jaxson Dart (134.2), Marcus Mariota (109.1), Jayden Daniels (99.1), Lamar Jackson (136.7) and C.J. Stroud (126.7) have had their way with the defense. Coming up next is Green Bay's Jordan Love, followed by Philadelphia's Jalen Hurts. It won't get easier.

Most surprising performance: For all of the defensive struggles in the first month of the season, the Cowboys' third-down defense had improved greatly during the previous two games. The Baltimore Ravens converted 3 of 9 tries in Week 3, and the Texans went 3-of-10 last week. By the end of the Buccaneers' first drive Thursday, they had four third-down conversions. And they did it with an undrafted rookie quarterback making just his second start. Tampa finished 7 of 13. Just when it seems as though the Cowboys have stopped one hole on defense, another pops up.

Stat to know: Through five games, Javonte Williams has six rushing touchdowns, capping the Cowboys' only first-quarter drive with a 1-yard run. Williams is the second Cowboy with at least six rushing scores in the first five games. Emmitt Smith did it twice (seven in 1994, nine in 1995), and Calvin Hill had six in 1971. Williams had a career-high 11 rushing touchdowns in his first season with the Cowboys last year. -- Todd Archer

Next game: at Green Bay Packers (Oct. 18)

stories.headline: 76ers' Embiid calls 'not true' LeBron report 'unfortunate'
stories.summary: Joel Embiid said a recent report about LeBron James getting on him about being late to practice "is not true" and caused him to wonder why he was targeted.
stories.body:
NEW YORK -- Philadelphia 76ers center Joel Embiid said a recent report about LeBron James getting on him about being late to practice "is not true" and caused him to wonder why he was subject to the outside scrutiny.

"It sucks, but what can you do? It's unfortunate," Embiid said after making his preseason debut in Philadelphia's 114-108 loss to the Brooklyn Nets on Thursday night. "I don't know where that came from. It never happened. ... I think we just got to focus on ourselves. There's going to be a lot of outside noise to pull us apart from what we're supposed to be and what we're supposed to accomplish. So, it's important that we stay together and we keep our [head] down."

During the fourth quarter of the Sixers' 120-97 win over the New York Knicks on Monday, longtime play-by-play announcer Mike Breen detailed on the MSG Networks broadcast what he had heard about James reacting to Embiid not making it onto the practice court on time.

"Somebody told me before the game that they were out ready to practice, and Joel Embiid walked out on the court a couple of minutes late, and LeBron let him hear it," Breen said on the broadcast.

James called the report "lies" on his Instagram account Tuesday. Breen later apologized.

"Those type of things, I can't understand," Embiid said. "One, it is not true, but then again, it's like, 'Why me?' ... I guess I'm Joel Embiid. I've been in that situation. I don't usually talk when it comes to those [rumors]. So, it feels like I'm an easy target.

"But yeah, as long as we know who we are [we will be OK] and we just got to stick together."

Embiid struggled against the Nets, scoring eight points on 1-for-5 shooting with three rebounds, three assists and eight turnovers in 24 minutes.

"Obviously, it's the preseason, especially for me," Embiid said. "I got to do a better job of taking care of the ball. But [it was the] first game, my first few games usually every year [are like this]. So yeah, it's going to take a few games to get going and just got to do a better job."

stories.headline: Connelly's SO goal lifts Golden Knights past Maple Leafs 4-3 after rallying from a 3-goal deficit
stories.summary: — Trevor Connelly scored in the fifth round of the shootout and the Vegas Golden Knights came back from a three-goal deficit for a 4-3 victory over the Toronto Maple Leafs on Thursday night.
stories.body:
LAS VEGAS -- — Trevor Connelly scored in the fifth round of the shootout and the Vegas Golden Knights came back from a three-goal deficit for a 4-3 victory over the Toronto Maple Leafs on Thursday night.


The rookie beat Sergei Bobrovsky with a backhand-forehand move before Vegas goalie Adin Hill denied Toronto's John Tavares as Vegas rallied for its third consecutive victory.


Braeden Bowman also scored for Vegas in the shootout. Kirill Marchenko was Toronto’s only successful shooter as Hill recovered from the early barrage and kept the Maple Leafs scoreless through the second, third, and overtime periods.


Mark Stone, Brett Howden and Jack Eichel — on a penalty shot — scored for Vegas. Hill made 21 saves and stopped four of Toronto’s five shootout attempts.


Jack Roslovic, Easton Cowan and Nick Paul gave Toronto a 3-0 lead in the first period. Bobrovsky made 40 saves.


Roslovic opened the scoring 34 seconds into his 600th career game, slipping the puck between Hill’s pads and the post from the goal line for his 300th career point.


Cowan scored on a breakaway at 3:20, and Paul made it 3-0 at 8:37.


Stone started the comeback with a slap shot at 17:36 of the first period. Eichel assisted, extending his assist and point streaks to five games.


Howden tapped in Mitch Marner’s pass at 1:12 of the second before Eichel tied it on a penalty shot at 3:58.


Eichel has three goals and 12 points through five games.


Vegas outshot Toronto 43-24 but went 0 for 4 on the power play, its first game without a power-play goal this season.


UP NEXT
Maple Leafs: Visit Colorado on Saturday.


Golden Knights: Host Los Angeles on Saturday.

stories.headline: Saints AFLW coach steps down as club plans review
stories.summary: Embattled St Kilda AFLW coach Nick Dal Santo has stepped down amid the club's winless season.
stories.body:
Embattled St Kilda AFLW coach Nick Dal Santo has stepped down amid the club's winless season.

The last-placed Saints will conduct a review into their AFLW program, led by former Carlton football boss Brad Lloyd, in the wake of Dal Santo's departure.

Dal Santo, a St Kilda great as a player, was in his sixth season at the Saints and will coach his final game against Collingwood on Saturday, before departing.

"I've been giving a lot of thought to my future and whether continuing in this role was the right decision, both for myself and the program," Dal Santo said in a statement.

"Where we've been able to take this program is something I'll always be incredibly proud of.

"It's been a privilege to coach this group and help shape its formative years in the competition.

"I have a strong love for this club, I wanted to contribute to women's football, and with a daughter of my own, it's great to see a pathway for young females with football ambitions.

"I'm looking forward to finishing my time as coach alongside the group this weekend and wish them every success for what comes next."

The Saints will have three games left in the season after Saturday, when they will attempt to amend their unwanted record of being the only winless team in the competition.

"Nick has made a significant contribution to our AFLW program across six seasons and will always be an important part of our football club," St Kilda chief executive Carl Dilena said in a statement

"His care, commitment and leadership have been unwavering, and we thank him for everything he has given to the program, including leading the team to its maiden final's appearance last season.

"We look forward to recognising Nick's contribution this weekend as he leads the team one final time in front of our members and supporters at RSEA Park."

Lloyd will lead the review, via Apogee Sports, during the remainder of the season, while the Saints start their hunt for their next coach.

"Our ambition is to be a consistently competitive and respected club that can contend with the best in the competition," Dilena said.

"We want to give our AFLW program every chance to achieve this and that means identifying where we need to improve, investing in the right areas and acting with urgency."

stories.headline: When can Kimi Antonelli win the F1 title? Earliest date, points needed and remaining races
stories.summary: With an 84-point lead in the drivers' standings, it is looking increasingly likely that Kimi Antonelli will be crowned F1's youngest world champion in the next two months.
stories.body:
With an 84-point lead in the drivers' standings, it is looking increasingly likely that Kimi Antonelli will be crowned F1's youngest world champion in the next two months.

Determining when and where that coronation will likely take place is much harder to say, not least because there are still question marks over how many races remain in the F1 calendar.

Antonelli's closest competitor, Mercedes teammate George Russell, saw his title chances take a critical blow when he retired from Sunday's Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia with an engine failure, and a related grid penalty at this weekend's Singapore Grand Prix will make his job tougher still.

Meanwhile, Lewis Hamilton, Charles Leclerc, Lando Norris and Max Verstappen all remain in mathematical contention for this year's championship, but face even tougher routes to the title than Russell due to their greater points deficits.

When could Antonelli win his first title?
In theory, the earliest Antonelli could seal the title is at the U.S. Grand Prix in Austin later this month. In order to do so, he would need to grow his gap over Russell by 42 points in two race weekends, while outscoring Lewis Hamilton in third place by 20 points.

- Singapore Grand Prix 2026: Race start time, how to watch

- Valtteri Bottas cycles 400km from Malaysia to Singapore

- F1 cars to get software update after Malaysia 'bug'

Even with extra points on offer at the sprint race in Singapore this weekend, such a scenario would likely require victories for Antonelli and further retirements for Russell, while ensuring Hamilton is not in the fight for second place on the podium behind Antonelli. In addition, an Austin crowning would require Antonelli to make sure he is not outscored by three points by Leclerc, and six points by both Norris and Verstappen.

What does Antonelli need to claim the title?
Perhaps the easiest way to look at Antonelli's title run-in is that he needs to score 100 points over the remaining races to ensure he ends up as champion -- regardless of what any of his rivals manage.

With seven grands prix and a sprint race currently scheduled on the calendar, that route could be achieved with multiple different result combinations -- but for ease of an example, third place at every remaining race would comfortably see Antonelli over the line even if Russell wins at all seven grands prix and the sprint.

F1's rules state that if multiple drivers are tied on points, a countback of victories will decide who emerges on top. If the number of victories are also even, it then goes to second places, third places, fourth place, and so on. Currently, Antonelli has eight victories to Russell's three, although Russell has four second places to Antonelli's three. It's unlikely those countbacks will come into play, but it's why, currently, Antonelli needs 100 points rather than 99 to put the title entirely beyond Russell's grasp.

But how many races are actually left?
The situation is further complicated by question marks hanging over the final two races of the season in Qatar and Abu Dhabi. F1 has made clear that it intends to finish the season as scheduled, but the ongoing war between the United States and Iran has the potential to force the cancellation of both rounds.

The same conflict led the cancellation of the Saudi Arabian Grand Prix in April, while Bahrain took the unusual approach of hosting its round 4,000 miles away from the island kingdom in Malaysia last weekend.

If Qatar and Abu Dhabi are also cancelled, F1's contingency plan is to host the final round of the season in Imola. Such a scenario would remove 25 of the potential points on offer, meaning Antonelli would only need 75 points between now and the end of the season to be crowned champion. Austin would still be the earliest round at which he could clinch the title, but it would come with a more achievable target of outscoring Russell by 17 points across the Singapore and U.S. race weekends rather than 42.

stories.headline: Silva rises in P4P women's top 10, making most of golden opportunity
stories.summary: After winning UFC women's flyweight title, Silva rises in ESPN's P4P top 10.
stories.body:
The women's flyweight division might be the most stacked weight class in the UFC, and Natalia Silva wears the gold.

Silva was too fast, too precise and too elusive for Wang Cong in the UFC 332 main event on Saturday, and as a result, the 29-year-old from Brazil captured the vacant 125-pound title. She moves up one position to No. 4 in the ESPN women's pound-for-pound rankings.

Silva is one of seven flyweights in the women's top 10. The division with the next most pound-for-pound elites is lightweight, with three fighters in the men's rankings.

The top two fighters on the women's list are Valentina Shevchenko, who vacated the UFC title last month while healing shoulder and back injuries, and Zhang Weili, a two-time former strawweight titlist who last fought at flyweight, in an unsuccessful challenge of Shevchenko in November.

Aside from Silva, there are three other UFC flyweights in the top 10 (Alexa Grasso, Manon Fiorot and Erin Blanchfield), and the rankings also include PFL 125-pounder Dakota Ditcheva.

UFC women's bantamweight champion Kayla Harrison has been missing from these rankings for the past few months because, with no fights since June 2025, she is ineligible. But Harrison will return from neck surgery to defend her title against former two-division champion and consensus GOAT Amanda Nunes at UFC 334 on Nov. 14.

For the ESPN divisional MMA rankings, click here.

Note: Results are current; rankings are as of Oct. 7. To be eligible for the rankings, a fighter must have competed over the past 12 months or must have an upcoming fight booked. Fighters who have been dropped for inactivity can be reinstated only after they compete.

Women's pound-for-pound rankings

1. Valentina Shevchenko

UFC flyweight

Record: 26-4-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Zhang Weili, Nov. 15, 2025

Next: TBA

Shevchenko's dominance came under question in 2022 and 2023, when she went 1-1-1 in a trilogy with Alexa Grasso. Boy, does that feel like a long time ago now. Shevchenko more than reasserted herself as the best flyweight in the world, and then she established herself as the No. 1 woman in the world, period. It wasn't surprising that she beat Zhang, but it was surprising how easy she made it look. Shevchenko is out injured, however, so she has vacated her UFC title, which Natalia Silva captured by beating Wang Cong at UFC 332. When Shevchenko is healed up, she'll be looking to take back the belt.

2. Zhang Weili

UFC flyweight / strawweight

Record: 26-4

Last: L (UD) vs. Valentina Shevchenko, Nov. 15, 2025

Next: TBA

It's hard to move up in weight, especially at the highest level. That sounds like it should be obvious, but Zhang had been dominant at 115 pounds for so long, some of us might have taken for granted how big of a challenge moving to 125 would be. UFC 322 was a bad night for Zhang, but she doesn't have many. And if she decides to stay at flyweight, it certainly seems reasonable to believe she'll fare better in the future.

3. Cris Cyborg

PFL featherweight champion

Record: 30-2, 1 NC

Last: W (UD) vs. Ketlen Vieira, Aug. 22

Next: TBA

It had been a while since Cyborg had fought an elite opponent in MMA until she met Larissa Pacheco in 2024. That was a legitimate matchup -- and many within the industry were predicting Cyborg's downfall. Instead, she took out the PFL's two-weight champion, upending all of Pacheco's momentum. One of the original pioneers of women's MMA is once again a champion after getting her second career submission at PFL Lyon in December. The PFL promoted her fight with Vieira as a retirement bout, but after her win Cyborg did not sound like someone who is done fighting.

4. Natalia Silva

UFC flyweight champion

Previous ranking: 5

Record: 21-5-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Wang Cong, Oct. 3

Next: TBA

Silva was looking every bit the part of a future UFC champion following a dominant display against Alexa Grasso at UFC 315 and a victory over Rose Namajunas at UFC 324. And now she has fulfilled that expectation, beating Wang at UFC 332 to win the belt vacated by injured Valentina Shevchenko. Silva's stick-and-move style has frustrated even the highest level of opponent, and she's got youth on her side as she won't turn 30 until 2027.

5. Mackenzie Dern

UFC strawweight champion

Previous ranking: 4

Record: 17-5

Last: W (UD) vs. Gillian Robertson, Aug. 15

Next: TBA

Dern's rise to the 115-pound throne was truly a changing of the guard. She is the division's first first-time champion since 2019, because the previous three champs -- Zhang Weili, Carla Esparza and Rose Namajunas -- all were in their second reigns. Dern, nearly a decade into her MMA career after multiple jiu-jitsu world championships, has won four fights in a row, including a dominant performance against a fellow grappling-heavy fighter, Robertson, in her first title defense.

6. Alexa Grasso

UFC flyweight

Record: 18-5-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Manon Fiorot, Sept. 12

Next: TBA

Grasso went nearly three years without winning a fight, but her 2023 win right before the skid was a huge one, a submission of Valentina Shevchenko for the UFC title. What followed were two more fights with Shevchenko -- a draw, then a loss -- and then a loss to Natalia Silva. But she reasserted herself with a finish of Maycee Barber in March, then got the best of Fiorot, a fellow title contender, at Noche UFC to put herself in position for another title shot.

7. Dakota Ditcheva

PFL flyweight

Record: 16-0

Last: W (UD) vs. Denise Kielholtz, July 31

Next: TBA

Not only did Ditcheva win the PFL's flyweight season in 2024, but she did so in spectacular fashion -- a TKO finish over Taila Santos, who once challenged for a UFC title. Ditcheva fought only once in 2025, dominating Sumiko Inaba in the co-main event of the first PFL Champions Series card in Cape Town, South Africa. She then spent over a year on the sideline, healing injuries to both hands, before returning at PFL New York with a dominant win over Kielholtz.

8. Manon Fiorot

UFC flyweight

Record: 13-3

Last: L (UD) vs. Alexa Grasso, Sept. 12

Next: TBA

Fiorot had handled everyone the UFC put in front of her -- except the champion, Valentina Shevchenko, who defeated the Frenchwoman at UFC 315 in May 2025. But then, with another title shot within her grasp, Fiorot ran into Grasso, a former champion, at Noche UFC and lost a competitive fight.

9. Erin Blanchfield

UFC flyweight

Record: 14-2

Last: W (Sub2) vs. Tracy Cortez, Nov. 15, 2025

Next: Oct. 17 vs. Jasmine Jasudavicius

Her rise toward the top of the division was derailed by a March 2024 loss to Manon Fiorot, but Blanchfield bounced back with two straight wins, including one over two-time former strawweight champion Rose Namajunas in November 2024. If she wins her upcoming bout with Jasudavicius, a fellow top-10 flyweight contender, Blanchfield would inch ever closer to a title shot.

10. Tatiana Suarez

UFC strawweight

Record: 12-1

Last: W (Sub2) vs. Loopy Godínez, April 11

Next: TBA

If Suarez is still feeling the effects of last year's humbling defeat to Zhang Weili in a title challenge, she certainly didn't show it at UFC 327, overcoming early adversity to thrash Godinez, a fellow top-10 strawweight. Suarez is going to be a tough out for anyone at 115 pounds.

How our panel voted
Brett Okamoto: 1. Valentina Shevchenko; 2. Zhang Weili; 3. Mackenzie Dern; 4. Natalia Silva; 5. Cris Cyborg; 6. Alexa Grasso; 7. Manon Fiorot; 8. Dakota Ditcheva; 9. Erin Blanchfield; 10. Tatiana Suarez.

Carlos Contreras Legaspi: 1. Shevchenko; 2. Cyborg; 3. Silva; 4. Zhang; 5. Dern; 6. Grasso; 7. Ditcheva; 8. Suarez; 9. Fiorot; 10. Blanchfield.

Andrew Davis: 1. Shevchenko; 2. Zhang; 3. Cyborg; 4. Silva; 5. Dern; 6. Grasso; 7. Ditcheva; 8. Fiorot; 9. Blanchfield; 10. Suarez.
